Several published posts mention negative keywords in one line (how-much-google-ads-cost-small-business, hvac-marketing, roofing-marketing, lead-generation-for-contractors, spanish-language-google-ads-for-local-business); none explains how they work. This post owns the how: what a negative keyword is, how to read the search terms report, which searches a local service business usually blocks (jobs, DIY, free, wrong service, wrong area), match types for negatives and a routine for reviewing the report. Do not repeat the trade specific lists from the HVAC and roofing posts: link them. Registered IDs: T9 and T10 (you pay at most the max CPC, usually less; the auction considers relevance), T11 (landing page experience and ad relevance as diagnostics), T14 (avg CPC), T16 (Keyword Planner). NEW SOURCES NEEDED, register before writing: the Google Ads Help page 'About negative keywords' and the page on the search terms report (candidate URLs from memory, confirm by WebFetch and keep only literal text: https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2453972 and https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2472708). Confirm in the negative keywords page what each match type does before describing it. NO source for how much spend negative keywords save, for the share of irrelevant clicks or for CPC by industry: write none and promise no savings. Calendar readiness B. Runbook rules: no timeframe, cost range or statistic without a source registered in docs/blog-fontes-verificadas.md; neutral voice, no invented Etuos experience.

items.title: Do You Need a Separate Web Page for Every City You Serve?
secondary_keywords: location pages for service area business
do i need a page for each city
items.notes: New spoke created for the October calendar (the open planned topic 'what makes a service page convert', re-angled to the question owners actually ask). Decision guide: when a page per city or per service earns its place (real differences in service, proof, people, neighborhoods, FAQs) and when it becomes a near duplicate that only swaps the city name. The local SEO complete guide has one paragraph telling owners to build a unique page per city; this post owns the how and the limits. Keep it apart from service-area-business-google-business-profile (the Business Profile side: hiding the address, up to 20 service areas, S20) and from website-not-getting-calls (conversion diagnosis): link each in one line. Registered IDs: S20 (service areas on the profile, up to 20), S10 (distance is a ranking factor, no way to pay for rank), S18 (service area businesses hide the address; the service area should not extend farther than about 2 hours of driving time), S25 (the language of a page comes from its visible content, for the bilingual case). NEW SOURCES NEEDED, register before writing: Google Search Central spam policies, the doorway abuse definition (https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies, confirm the literal text by WebFetch) and Google's guidance on helpful, people-first content (https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content). NO source that more city pages rank better, for how many pages are too many or for any ranking effect of a service radius: do not claim any. Say plainly that a page per city is not required and that proximity still limits where a business can rank. Calendar readiness B. Runbook rules: no timeframe, cost range or statistic without a source registered in docs/blog-fontes-verificadas.md; neutral voice, no invented Etuos experience.

items.title: Med Spa Marketing: How to Book High Ticket Treatments Without Discounting
secondary_keywords: how to get med spa clients
items.notes: PARKED on 10/27/2026: regulated sector with no registered source for health ad policies. Its 10/30 slot was replaced by an A item. Resume only with Google's health ad policy registered or with no policy claim at all. | Industry playbook for an industry in the city data (med spas and aesthetics in Miami and Atlanta, src/data/cidades/en.ts). High ticket with a long consideration cycle, so the metric is consultations booked, not clicks, and the post is about trust: profile and photos of the space, review handling, a consultation page that answers the fear instead of selling the discount. Policy matters here and must be respected in the copy: Google and Meta restrict health and personal care advertising and reject claims about outcomes, so NO before and after promises, no medical claims, no treatment result language, no price. Registered sources: S5 and S9 (review behavior and the 4.5 star threshold), S10 (local ranking), S18 and S21 (profile guidelines), T9, T10 and T11 (auction and Quality Score as a diagnostic). Library gap: no verified cost per lead or conversion benchmark for this industry, so keep cost talk qualitative. PROHIBITED: client names, invented cases, prices, guarantees, timeframes. No em dash. Calendar readiness C (regulated industry, owner decision first). The note above says Google and Meta restrict health and personal care advertising: that is a factual claim with NO registered source, so the post may not state it until the policy pages are registered (candidate: Google Advertising Policies Help, Healthcare and medicines, https://support.google.com/adspolicy/answer/176031, confirm the literal text; Meta's advertising standards on personal health live on transparency.meta.com, which is NOT in docs/blog-dominios-confiaveis.md, so add the domain there first or write no Meta policy claim). Absolute copy rules: no medical, safety or outcome claim, no before and after, no treatment names with benefits, no price, no comparison of procedures. Frame everything around trust, profile, review handling and consultation page clarity. Needs Lin: approve the approach (policy sources or none) and confirm that the post may mention med spa as one of the 13 industries only in the neutral voice. NO source for cost per lead, consultation conversion or treatment demand. Runbook rules: no timeframe, cost range or statistic without a source registered in docs/blog-fontes-verificadas.md; neutral voice, no invented Etuos experience.
